summary: Build the dense actual-coordinate flux matrix for an R,Z node grid.

capability: Build the dense actual-coordinate flux matrix for an R,Z node grid.
operation: matching R,Z grids -> target-row/source-column psi response
discovery.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with zero diagonal for active source nodes.
discovery.geometry: Finite rectilinear or irregular two-dimensional coordinate arrays.
discovery.boundary: Axis rows and zero-radius source columns are zero, and duplicate positive-radius nodes are rejected.

identity.direction: matching R,Z grids to target-row/source-column psi response
identity.definition: Flatten matching R,Z arrays in C order and evaluate every actual target/source pair.
identity.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with zero diagonal for active source nodes.
identity.geometry: Finite rectilinear or irregular 2-D coordinate arrays.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; matrix entries Wb/rad/A.
identity.boundary: Axis rows and zero-radius source columns are zero; duplicate positive-radius nodes are rejected.
assumptions: Inputs are finite real matching 2-D arrays.
The matrix is dense and uses the explicit zero-self convention.

outputs.name: G
outputs.description: Flux response matrix with target rows/source columns Returned directly as the callable's single positional value (one float64 (R.size, R.size) matrix); it is not a field of a mapping.

preconditions: Inputs are finite real matching 2-D arrays.
The matrix is dense and uses the explicit zero-self convention.
supported: Irregular/asymmetric coordinates, permutation covariance, axis limits, and duplicate/complex failures.
excluded: Finite-conductor self-inductance, extreme-scale qualification, and equilibrium claims.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for malformed, complex, nonfinite, negative-radius, or duplicate active nodes.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError from an unrepresentable kernel response propagates.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct matrix evaluation.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No matrix is returned after validation or kernel failure.

example.description: Build a dense matrix from a 3x3 irregular R,Z mesh.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.electromagnetism import get_gpsi
R,Z=np.meshgrid([.4,.8,1.2],[-.5,0.,.9])
G=get_gpsi(R,Z)
assert G.shape==(9,9) and np.all(np.diag(G)==0)
example.expected: The result is a finite (9,9) matrix with an exactly zero diagonal.

scope: Original irregular and unchanged uniform geometry
Independent asymmetric heldout integral and permutation oracle

Independent reference (tests/electromagnetism/_ideal_ring_reference.py): off-diagonal entries are recomputed from the complement-free AgM elliptic flux, which evaluates the parameter m directly rather than the complement 1-m used here, cross-certified against direct Biot-Savart quadrature at 1e-22 relative. A second, fully independent statement is the reciprocity of the mutual flux G[i, j] = G[j, i], which this code does not build in - each column is evaluated in one direction only - so a wrong modulus, a wrong distance sum or a swapped (2-m)K-2E pair breaks it while a single-direction quadrature comparison survives.

Implementation relation: G is the dense target-as-source matrix of the unit-weight ideal-filament flux, ordered by the C-order flattening of the 2-D (R, Z) inputs, with psi in Wb/rad per ampere, mu0/(4 pi) = 1e-7 exactly, the height difference Z - Z0, distinct positive-radius nodes required, and the diagonal set to zero by the discrete self convention.

Test matrix (tests/electromagnetism/test_loop_flux_matrix_evidence.py, 5 cases): reciprocity over every active pair of an irregular 5 by 4 grid that includes an on-axis node and targets on both sides of the branch cutover; every off-diagonal entry against the reference; the exact zero diagonal and the exact zero rows and columns of a zero-radius node; permutation covariance under a fixed node permutation together with the C-order flattening convention; and every rejection channel. Boundary cases are the axis node and the coincident-node rejection; non-finite and shape failures are in the failure matrix.

Precision budget, fixed before the comparison ran: 64 eps = 1.42e-14 relative per entry, and 2 x 64 eps for the reciprocity difference because the two entries are two independent evaluations of one mathematical quantity and each may carry the full per-entry budget. The reference contributes at most 1e-22 relative.

Failure matrix, one executable assertion per contract channel in failure_semantics: ValueError for a complex array, a non-2-D or mismatched shape, a negative radius, a nonfinite entry, and duplicate active nodes; an unrepresentable response is covered by the shared kernel contract that reports FloatingPointError. No matrix is returned on any of these paths.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent numerical evidence for the named grid, the mutual-flux reciprocity law that the code does not build in, and exact structural facts (zero diagonal, inactive nodes, permutation covariance, C-order flattening). Not finite-conductor self-inductance and not an arbitrary-domain bound.
known_limitations: Zero-self is a limited discrete model
No finite wire, singular pair or physical equilibrium solution claim

Reciprocity is asserted for the named grid with a two-budget bound rather than bitwise, because the two directions are evaluated separately; the matrix is dense and quadratic in the node count, so the evidence covers one 20-node grid and not larger assemblies.

basis.statement: Independent numerical evidence for the named grid, the mutual-flux reciprocity law that the code does not build in, and exact structural facts (zero diagonal, inactive nodes, permutation covariance, C-order flattening).
